title: About HART
lede: HART Railroad is a model railroad set on Neville Island, the industrial island in the Ohio River just below Pittsburgh. The island, its plants and the railroads that served them are real. HART is the one piece we made up: an imagined successor to the island's own short line.

sections.heading: The island
paragraphs: Neville Island was farmland until about 1900. Within a generation it had furnaces, coke ovens and chemical plants, nearly all of them shipping by rail, with barges working the river alongside.

For nearly a century the Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley switched those plants and handed their cars to the larger roads, until it shut down in 1994. Much of what we know about it comes from the people who worked it, and their stories are a big part of why this layout exists.

sections.heading: Our railroad
paragraphs: HART picks up where the P&OV left off. Its Pittsburgh & Chartiers Valley Division switches the island's plants and trades cars with the connecting railroads at either end of the island.
The customers on the layout are plants that worked on the island, and their traffic follows what they shipped and received. Where we've bent history to fit the room, the Industries pages say so.

sections.heading: Running it like a railroad
paragraphs: The island has always been a squeeze. Cars come in from both ends, meet in one small yard, and go back out to the plants and the connections. A session works the same way: several jobs at once, all needing the same few tracks, so they have to be worked around each other.

That squeeze is what makes it interesting. The yardmaster decides what gets sorted first. The dispatcher decides who gets the main and who waits. Crews work out their own moves at the plants and talk to each other to get it done. It runs at the pace of a real switching railroad: slowly, and with plenty of conversation.

Sessions are a few hours with friends. You don't need to know the railroad beforehand. Each crew gets a sheet for its job, and there's a briefing before anyone moves a train. The railroad is still being built, and most sessions change something about how it runs.

sections.heading: On this site
paragraphs: History & Industries is for anyone curious about the island. It holds what we have learned about the P&OV and the plants it served, with old photographs, advertisements and clippings credited to their sources where we could find them.
Operations is for the people who come to run trains. It has a primer for first-timers, the paperwork used at the layout, and a look around the layout room and the equipment that works it.
